items.title: Operation Toofan: Kerala police struggle to deal with addicts
items.summary: Kerala’s anti-narcotics campaign ‘Operation Toofan’, completed 100 days on September 9. The numbers are staggering: After the start of the campaign, till September 17, police have arrested 11,776 people in 10,918 cases. They also seized 23925.120 grams of MDMA and nearly 1457 kg of cannabis. But inside Kerala’s prisons and police stations, officers are confronting a different side of the drug problem: people exhibiting severe withdrawal symptoms, becoming violent in police stations and prisons, sometimes injuring themselves or others, and returning to drug use soon after they are released. One reason for this, according to investigators and mental health professionals, is the absence of protocols to identify what they have consumed or address their addiction when people are arrested with small quantities. Is Kerala’s war on drugs holistic? Aalam* was shaking and struggling to control himself while in police custody after being picked up during an Operation Toofan search. The company's longer-term vision is for every lawyer to work alongside their own team of agents. These agents would prepare the morning brief and cause list before court, keep track of matters and deadlines across a team, prioritise and draft what comes out of the day's hearings, and turn changes agreed in a meeting into a revised draft. For a law firm, the result is an AI-native practice running alongside its lawyers. Every lawyer has agents producing finished work, and lawyers spend their time on judgement, strategy and final review. 8rney places approval controls around any action that may send, file or overwrite work. items.title: Half of Bengaluru East PGs inspected are illegal, GBA tells Karnataka HC
items.summary: Nearly half of the paying guest (PG) accommodations inspected in Bengaluru East are operating illegally, the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has told the Karnataka High Court. Of around 5,000 PG accommodations inspected in the East Zone, nearly 2,500 were found to be operating without proper licences, sanctioned building plans or fire safety clearances, advocate B S Karthikeyan, appearing for the GBA, told the court. The areas covered by the inspections include Whitefield, Mahadevapura, KR Puram, Indiranagar and CV Raman Nagar, which are home to several IT companies and multinational firms. Karthikeyan said notices were being issued to the owners of the illegal PGs. The GBA has also filed caveats before the High Court and jurisdictional civil courts to ensure that PG owners do not obtain ex parte interim stays without the Authority being heard. He said necessary orders would be passed at the earliest after giving the concerned parties an opportunity to respond. Where constructions are found to violate zoning regulations or building bye-laws, demolition would be undertaken if necessary, he added. items.title: Can Customs prohibit import of sex toys as obscene articles? Calcutta High Court to decide
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court has agreed to hear a petition challenging the Customs Department's decision to prohibit the import of sex toys into India, on the ground that they are "obscene articles." [ M/s Pracha Aalloy Private Limited v. Union of India & Ors. ] Justice Smita Das Dey noted that the question warrants consideration by the High Court as the Customs authorities appeared to have made its decision based on subjective morality, which has in turn affected the importer's right to trade. "When a statutory authority acts completely outside the boundaries of objective law and enters the realm of subjective morality thereby severely affecting a citizen’s fundamental right to trade, the High Court will not shut its doors. The present case involves systematic misrepresentation of trade regulations across various custom houses, which necessitates and authoritative judicial pronouncements rather than a routine departmental appeal. The precise statutory basis for the alleged prohibition, as also the basis for invoking Section 111(m) of the [Customs] Act, therefore, requires consideration ", the Court said in its order. items.title: Karnataka High Court quashes criminal case against Pearson Education's former in-house counsel
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has quashed criminal proceedings against former in-house legal counsel of Pearson Education/ Dorling Kindersley (India) Pvt Ltd, Prashant Kumar Joshi [Prashant Kumar Joshi v State of Karnataka]. By way of an order passed on September 11, Justice HP Sandesh quashed the criminal proceedings against Joshi in a case concerning legal metrology violations by Pearson Education. The Court said that Joshi was not a nominated personnel of the company (under Section 49 of the Legal Metrology Act), responsible for the company's business and conduct. The Court ruled that criminalising the former in-house counsel without the company being a party to the proceedings, would amount to an abuse of process of law. "Nothing is stated in the complaint that this petitioner was in charge of the affairs of the company and he being shown as General Manager (Legal), the question of initiating the criminal prosecution against this petitioner is nothing but an abuse of process, which amounts to miscarriage of justice," the order said. items.title: Karnataka advocate gets one-day jail term for drunken outburst in court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on September 11 sentenced a 51-year-old advocate, Pankaj Kaushik, to one day’s simple imprisonment, till the rising of the court, for criminal contempt after he misbehaved before a civil court in Karwar in 2022 while in an inebriated condition. A division bench of Justice Anu Sivaraman and Justice Venkatesh Naik T also imposed a fine of Rs 2,000 on Kaushik and directed that he be taken into custody immediately to serve the sentence, according to Indian Express. “We are of the clear opinion that if conduct of this nature is not punished, sociopaths like the accused are likely to repeat such offences with impunity which would endanger the rule of law and the judicial system as a whole,” the bench observed. The contempt proceedings stemmed from an incident on April 20, 2022, at the court of Shrinivas Patil, then additional civil judge and judicial magistrate first class-II in Karwar, Uttara Kannada district. On the day, at around 3.30 pm, a senior counsel was addressing arguments before Judge Patil when Kaushik interrupted and insisted that his case be taken up. items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Yet another accused has been arrested in the custodial death case of Gade Sai Krishna in Vijayawada. After absconding for nearly three months, the accused Suresh reportedly surrendered before the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing Sai Krishna’s custodial torture and death case on Thursday, September 17. A resident of Vijayawada’s Satyanarayanapuram, Suresh was allegedly handling financial transactions for Circle Inspector (CI) SSVV Nagaraju, the main accused in the case. Suresh was named accused no. 4 in Sai Krishna’s case. The SIT had already arrested CI Nagaraju, four constables, a home guard of the Krishnalanka police station and a medical practitioner in the alleged custodial torture and murder case. Gade Sai Krishna was picked up on May 6 by the Krishnalanka police from Markapuram, a town nearly 300 km from Vijayawada. A 25-year-old with a criminal record, Sai Krishna is alleged to have been tortured and murdered by Krishnalanka CI Nagaraju.
